title: Insights into the Biotech Industry: What is Regulatory Affairs?
html:
Hi everyone! I’m Ben (Leung, Ho-bank), VP of Regulatory Affairs at SurgicGuide.

So, what exactly is regulatory affairs?

In the biotech and medical technology industry, regulatory affairs is essentially about connecting science and innovation with the regulatory requirements needed to bring a product to patients.

At SurgicGuide, my role involves thinking about questions such as: What regulatory pathway might our AI-integrated FLIM System follow? What evidence do we need to generate? What information needs to be included in a regulatory submission? And how do we make sure our development plans are aligned with regulatory expectations?

It’s not simply about preparing paperwork. Regulatory considerations can influence product development, clinical studies, risk management, quality systems, and market access from an early stage.

One of the most interesting parts of the job is working with different teams. I regularly communicate with scientists, engineers, clinicians, and product developers to make sure regulatory requirements are considered alongside the technology itself.

And because regulations differ between countries, regulatory affairs also has an international dimension. A product strategy that works in one market may need to be adapted for another.

For me, regulatory affairs is about helping innovative technologies make the journey from the laboratory to real-world use — responsibly and with the right evidence behind them.

— Ben

Leung, Ho-bank

VP, Regulatory Affairs

SurgicGuide Limited
